description: The plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—for a model evaluated on the GPQA dataset, as referenced in the paper “Feedback Friction: LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback.” The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” spans from 0.91 to 0.99 in linear increments of 0.01, representing the model’s self-assessed confidence before feedback. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 in linear steps of 0.2, indicating the proportion of correct responses. The blue solid line with circle markers and error bars represents Final Accuracy, which remains relatively high and stable across the confidence range, fluctuating between approximately 0.88 and 1.0. The orange dashed line with diamond markers and error bars shows Δ Accuracy (change in accuracy after feedback), which peaks near 0.67 at initial confidence 0.92, then declines sharply to below 0.1 by 0.98 before rising slightly to 0.15 at 0.99. The green dash-dot line with square markers and error bars depicts Initial Accuracy, which starts at ~0.36 at 0.91, dips to ~0.26 at 0.92, then rises steadily to ~0.85 at 0.98 before falling slightly to ~0.77 at 0.99. Error bars are present for all three lines, indicating variability in measurements.
